intersection.def: The joint event "A and B", written $A \cap B$ (the intersection of A and B), happens when both A and B happen. Its probability is the joint probability $P(A \cap B)$; in a two-way table it is one cell over the grand total.

mutually-exclusive.def: Two events are mutually exclusive, or disjoint, when they have no outcomes in common, so they cannot happen together: $P(A \cap B) = 0$. Then the probability that one or the other happens is $P(A) + P(B)$.
